messages:
ajay: heads up — saw a weird pattern this morning: cluster autoscaler spawned up five tiny timeslice nodes (1 GPU each, time-sliced) while we still had underutilized MIG 4g nodes. ended up with fragmented GPU capacity and >2x the expected spot churn. :frowning:

Tess: ouch. do you have the node labels/taints set for the timeslice vs MIG pools? autoscaler tends to treat them the same unless we isolate by launch template/labels.

ajay: we do label them, but many pods don't have nodeSelector; they just request gpu resource and rely on topologyHints from the runtime. looks like kube-scheduler packed onto timeslice nodes to satisfy pod anti-affinity, then ASG scaled because resource usage thresholds hit.

leo: can you paste the pod spec that got scheduled? curious about tolerations/affinity.

ajay: sure — minimal example:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: embed-worker
spec:
  containers:
  - name: worker
    image: redwood/embed:prod
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1
```
no nodeSelector, no toleration. scheduler chose timeslice pool nodes because they had room.

irene: that's the root cause — if pods don't express preference we get unpredictable packing across heterogeneous nodepools. two quick fixes: 1) mutate requests on admission to add nodeSelector/affinity based on workload class, or 2) change autoscaler config to prefer scaling MIG pool if a MIG label is present.

Tess: we already have an admission webhook prototype that injects nodeAffinity for "latency-critical" label. should we expand it to detect whether a pod would benefit from contiguous MIG slices vs time-slice?

leo: detection is tricky. but we can add an annotation like `redwood.gpu.prefer: mig` on deployments and let the webhook translate to affinity. avoids guessing.

ajay: +1 for annotation. short-term workaround: mark timeslice node pool with taint `gpu.slice=true:NoSchedule` and add a toleration only to low-priority batch pods. that forces autoscaler to only create timeslice nodes for batch workloads and keeps interactive/steady traffic on MIG nodes.

irene: also noticed autoscaler behaves badly when mixed instance types share the same ASG. when we have both mig-enabled VMs and timeslice-capable VMs in one ASG, CA can't pick exact instance type, so it overshoots. separate ASGs per GPU config (and per purchase option: spot vs on-demand) helps.

Tess: agreed. we should update the autoscaler config docs: recommend one nodepool per GPU runtime flavor + labels: `gpu.mode=mig|timeslice`, `spot=true|false`, and `gpu.slice.size=1|4`. then we can tune scale-down delays differently.

ajay: FYI this had a cost impact: extra 3 nodes for ~45m, ~0.6k in spot churn and wasted preemption work. I'll attach metrics from prometheus later.

autoscaler-bot: scaled up nodegroup timeslice-1g-eu-west by 4 instances at 1870012800 (reason: usageThreshold exceeded).

leo: proposed follow-ups:
- short: add `redwood.gpu.prefer` annotation and update webhook to inject nodeAffinity/toleration
- medium: split nodepools/ASGs by GPU config + spot flag
- long: update cluster-autoscaler heuristics or build a custom scheduler extender to account for GPU topology when deciding scaling actions

Tess: I'll open a PR for the webhook change and a runbook for nodepool partitioning. assignable?

ajay: I can take the runbook and the prometheus cost dump.

irene: I'll prototype the `prefer:mig` annotation handling in the webhook.

Tess: sweet. tagging this thread :spiral_note_pad: and will create issues. thanks everyone!
